strictLocalization.description: If true (default), missing localizations in referenced resources, prompt templates, or lexicon profiles are a preflight error. If false, they are warnings with defaultLanguage fallback.

firstPcmEnqueueTimeoutMs.description: Required budget from playback-slot acquisition through preparation and all transport attempts until the first successfully enqueued aligned PCM block. Empty chunks and retries do not renew it. Expiry is a technical failure with a local cue, not a user cancellation or automatic dialog restart.

firstPcmTimeoutEarconId.description: Required finite local negative cue requested once per timed-out logical playback. Higher feedback owners may separately announce the failure. Listening, success and looping cues are not valid failure feedback.

sessionLanguageOfferEnabled.description: Whether the session entry puts the guided language decision to the participant. Absent or false means the entry stays silent about language, which is the configuration a study run uses so every participant hears the same announcements.

resourceCatalog.description: Reference to the standalone voice resource catalog for session-setup texts, language names, generic UI speech resources, and modeled listening cues. On wake-only activation the surface enters the application catalog dialog immediately; its spoken announcement acknowledges the activation and precedes the actual selection-capture cue. A cue that means 'speak now' must occur only when that capture window opens.

promptCatalog.description: Reference to the standalone generic prompt catalog for form-dialog and privacy fallback templates.

lexiconCatalog.description: Reference to the standalone voice lexicon catalog for yes/no and politeness semantics.

wakeWordCatalog.description: Reference to the standalone wake-word catalog for modeled activation forms, recognition-only activation forms, and optional cross-cycle stitching for incomplete multi-word activation forms. On wake-word-gated voice surfaces, this catalog contributes the activation signal that must be evidenced after the modeled armed-listening cue has surfaced and before interruption candidates may become command attempts or command-failure outcomes. A contiguous leading sequence of complete modeled activation forms is one idempotent activation; only the full remainder after that sequence is downstream content. Wake word plus executable content in the same utterance remains valid and may seed the downstream surface-owned dialog directly. Wake-word-only activations make the generic surface enter the surface-owned application catalog dialog without a prefetched transcript, so it announces the available applications before opening its selection listening turn. Genuine silence in that dialog is non-terminal and opens a fresh capture window after audible no-input feedback; cancel and classified system-failure terminals retain their own modeled audible feedback. The wakeUtteranceWindow stitcher applies only to incomplete multi-word activation assembly and never replaces that wake-only entry into the catalog dialog.

wakeWordDetectorCatalog.description: Reference to the standalone wake-word detector catalog for modeled acoustic evidence profiles. This catalog never owns lexical activation meaning or same-utterance command semantics; it owns only detector identity, gating thresholds, lookback, warmup, and explicit lexical fallback reasons.

Id.description: Identifier: starts with letter/underscore, followed by alphanumerics, dots, dashes, or underscores.
